publications.headline: Major Breaches at Bell Canada, Radware, and Azure Highlight API Security Risks

articles.headline: EU Commission Confirms Data Leak from 'AI-Assisted' Attack
articles.summary: The European Commission has confirmed that an 'AI-assisted' cyberattack on its EU Academy online learning platform led to a data breach. The incident, first detected in October 2026, exposed the names and email addresses of users from outside EU institutions. The EU Academy website has been taken offline until January 2027 for remediation. While details are scarce, it is considered 'highly likely' that an AI penetration testing tool called ARTEX was used in the attack.

articles.headline: 1Password Discloses Security Breach; Customer Vaults Safe
articles.summary: Password manager 1Password disclosed a security incident on November 25, 2026, where an attacker compromised an employee's GitHub account to access backend systems. The breach, which began on November 19, exposed a limited amount of customer administrative data, including names and emails. 1Password asserts that its zero-knowledge architecture protected all customer vault data, passwords, and secret keys, which were not accessed. The company has revoked access, rotated credentials, and is cautioning users about potential phishing attempts.

articles.headline: Bell Canada Confirms Breach by 'Agentic' Hacker, Customer Data Stolen
articles.summary: Bell Canada confirmed a data breach on November 17, 2026, where an 'agentic threat actor,' possibly using AI tools, accessed a pre-production system. The incident compromised personal and business customer data from Bell and its subsidiaries, including names, addresses, and account details. Highly sensitive financial data was reportedly not accessed. Bell has contained the threat, notified law enforcement, and is in the process of informing affected customers.

articles.headline: New Ransomware Group 'Inception' Claims 1TB Data Theft from Verisk
articles.summary: A newly emerged ransomware group named 'Inception' has claimed responsibility for a major cyberattack against Verisk, a leading data analytics and risk assessment firm. In a leak site post on November 26, 2026, the group alleges it exfiltrated 1.01 TB of highly sensitive data, including millions of client insurance contracts, database records, and proprietary loss models. The claim, which mentions major Verisk clients, has not yet been confirmed by the company. The group has set a short deadline for contact before releasing the data.

articles.headline: Radware Breach Exposes Customer Cloud Keys Via Public API
articles.summary: Cybersecurity provider Radware suffered a data breach on November 19, 2026, after an internal Cloud WAF management API was left exposed to the internet without authentication. Attackers accessed the API, exfiltrating customer contact information and, for some, cloud storage credentials for AWS S3 and Azure Blob. Radware detected the access after ten hours and has since secured the API, but is urging affected customers to rotate their cloud keys immediately as they are reportedly being actively targeted.

articles.headline: Azure API Flaw Exploited to Steal Secrets from Energy Firms
articles.summary: Microsoft has patched a vulnerability in the classic tiers of Azure API Management (APIM) that was actively exploited to steal credentials and configuration secrets. The flaw, identified on November 18, 2026, allowed unauthorized access to management functions. Attackers targeted several organizations, including Norwegian energy firms Equinor and Skagerak Energi. Microsoft has closed the access path but warns that credentials may have been compromised and is urging affected customers to rotate all secrets stored in APIM.

articles.headline: CISA Adds 10 Exploited Flaws in Mitel, Juniper, Vates, & Danfoss
articles.summary: On November 25, 2026, CISA added ten actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to patch critical flaws in Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss products. The additions include a perfect 10.0 CVSS score vulnerability in Mitel MiCollab (CVE-2026-133323) allowing remote command injection, a 9.8 CVSS flaw in Juniper Session Smart Conductor (CVE-2026-103406), and an authentication bypass in Vates Xen Orchestra (CVE-2026-133469). These actions highlight immediate risks to communication, networking, virtualization, and industrial control systems.

articles.headline: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Hits 178 Major Websites
articles.summary: A significant supply chain attack on November 16, 2026, compromised Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform, allowing attackers to inject malicious JavaScript into the websites of 178 organizations. High-profile victims include the BBC, CNN, Zoom, and HSBC. The injected scripts were designed to steal payment data, session cookies, and cryptocurrency. Optimizely has since patched the exploited vulnerability and removed the malicious code, stating that less than 5% of its customers were affected.

publications.headline: AI Fuels Cyberattacks, Critical Flaws & Record Ransomware Emerge

articles.headline: UK NCSC Warns Agentic AI Frameworks Are Automating Cyberattacks
articles.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has issued a warning about a significant increase in AI-assisted cyberattacks since September 2026. Attackers are reportedly using agentic offensive frameworks, like ARTEX, to automate the discovery and exploitation of common, 'low-hanging fruit' security weaknesses such as exposed credentials, misconfigurations, and API flaws. This allows for attacks to proceed from discovery to exploitation in minutes.

articles.headline: AI-Assisted Campaign by GreyNoise13 Hits 22 Orgs via Check Point Flaws
articles.summary: A threat actor tracked as GreyNoise13 (GT13) has compromised at least 22 organizations globally in a sophisticated, AI-assisted hacking campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers since mid-October 2026. The attackers are leveraging a chain of critical vulnerabilities for initial access, including flaws in Check Point, Citrix, and Ivanti products, impacting critical sectors like energy, finance, and government across eight countries.

articles.headline: Attackers Deploy Autonomous AI Agents to Automate High-Speed Campaigns
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has uncovered a significant evolution in attack methodologies, observing over ten global campaigns where threat actors deployed autonomous AI agents to conduct intrusions. These 'agentic AI attackers,' typically Large Language Models (LLMs) with tool-using capabilities, operate at machine speed, compressing attack timelines from weeks to mere hours. The campaigns targeted diverse sectors, including government and manufacturing, initiating attacks via web shells on vulnerable applications. While the agents use standard tools, they leave distinct behavioral fingerprints, such as inhuman command velocity, structured command outputs, and conversational reasoning comments embedded in scripts, providing new avenues for detection.

articles.headline: CISA Adds 10 More Exploited Flaws to KEV from Danfoss, HPE, Mitel, Vates
articles.summary: On November 25, 2026, CISA added ten more vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, signaling active exploitation in the wild. The newly added flaws impact a diverse range of products from vendors including Danfoss, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), Mitel, and Vates. Federal agencies are mandated under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04 to prioritize patching these high-risk vulnerabilities.

articles.headline: Massive Data Leak Exposes Two Billion Credentials from Infostealer Ops
articles.summary: A cybersecurity researcher has discovered a massive, non-password-protected database on the public internet containing approximately two billion credentials. The discovery, made by Jeremiah Fowler and reported by ExpressVPN, is believed to be an aggregation of data harvested from widespread infostealer malware campaigns. The exposed data includes a vast collection of usernames and passwords in plaintext, posing a severe risk of account takeovers and credential stuffing attacks.

articles.headline: Ransomware Attacks Surge to Record High in Q3 2026 as New Groups Emerge
articles.summary: Ransomware attacks reached an unprecedented high in the third quarter of 2026, with 2,830 victims publicly named on data leak sites, according to a new report from Check Point Research. The quarter was marked by a significant proliferation of new and returning ransomware groups, leading to a more fragmented and less concentrated threat landscape. For the first time, the top ten most active gangs were responsible for less than half of all published attacks.

articles.headline: CISA Adds Actively Exploited Drupal, Optimizely, and AntiCsrf Flaws to KEV
articles.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation. The flaws include a remote code execution vulnerability in Drupal Core (CVE-2026-132165), a critical deserialization flaw in Idunno.AntiCsrf (CVE-2026-131914), and a state control issue in Optimizely Web Experimentation (CVE-2026-132224). Federal agencies are now under a strict deadline to remediate these high-risk vulnerabilities.

articles.headline: Critical Auth Bypass Flaw (CVE-2026-123903) Hits VMware vCenter
articles.summary: Broadcom has released patches for a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-123903) in VMware vCenter Server. The flaw, rated 9.8 on the CVSS scale, resides in the VMware Directory Service (vmdir) and could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to gain administrative access to the vCenter management layer. While there is no evidence of active exploitation yet, the disclosure follows a recently exploited zero-day in the same component, making immediate patching a top priority.

articles.headline: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free Flaw (CVE-2026-123633) Allows DoS, RCE
articles.summary: A critical use-after-free vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123633, has been discovered in the NGINX HTTP/2 implementation. The flaw can be triggered by an unauthenticated attacker sending a specially crafted, fragmented HTTP/2 request to a vulnerable server configured as a reverse proxy. Successful exploitation can cause a denial of service (DoS) by crashing the worker process. Researchers have also demonstrated that remote code execution (RCE) is possible by chaining the vulnerability with a separate memory disclosure bug, particularly when Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or bypassed. NGINX has released patches, and administrators are urged to upgrade affected systems immediately.

articles.headline: Two Critical GeoServer Flaws Actively Exploited for RCE
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting two critical vulnerabilities in the open-source GeoServer platform (CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243), chaining them together to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. The exploitation was observed in the wild by security firm watchTowr just one day after patches were released, prompting urgent warnings for administrators to update their instances or restrict access immediately.
